ui.legacy-blade-shell: Downgraded, not disabled: both hits stay visible in every report.
What the rule is right about: core has no Blade CP pages left, and a Blade page gets no
client-side Inertia navigation — every filter, sort and page change that leaves the listing
is a full document load rather than an SPA visit.
What it is wrong about here, against statamic/cms v6.26.0: the page does get breadcrumbs and
it does get shared props. `Statamic::nonInertiaPageData()` (src/Statamic.php:497-507) puts
`Inertia::getShared()` on the page object, and breadcrumbs are derived server-side from the
active nav item, which this addon registers. Verified in the studio playground: the CP
renders `/ Activity` in the global header and the Tools nav entry is active.
Why it stays: closing it means introducing a Vite build — package.json, @statamic/cms from
vendor, a committed dist/ plus a CI job that fails on drift, or the composer-dist-plugin
release-artifact path. This addon has 1.6k lines of PHP, no JS at all, and two read-only
screens. Core supports the Blade path deliberately (statamic.js:206-212 resolves
`NonInertiaPage` by compiling the yielded content as a Vue template inside the core Layout),
and that is exactly what makes the `<ui-*>` components below resolve. Both screens are now
built out of ui-header, ui-listing, ui-panel, ui-card, ui-badge, ui-button, ui-icon,
ui-empty-state-menu and ui-docs-callout, with no addon CSS at all.
Adopting a build toolchain for this addon is a decision for Adrian, not a hardening change.
testing.addon-testcase: Statamic\Testing\AddonTestCase cannot boot this addon. Its setUp() calls
`Nav::shouldReceive('build')`, which swaps the Nav facade for a strict Mockery mock; the
addon's bootAddon() then calls `Nav::extend()` and the mock throws
expectations were specified`. Reproduced on 2026-08-01 with a probe test before this entry
was written. AddonTestCase also never invokes bootAddon() itself, so the hand-rolled call
in tests/TestCase.php would have to stay either way.
The bed it would replace is not incidental: it runs the identical suite against real MySQL
via DB_DRIVER=mysql (phpunit.mysql.xml), because the column widths and InnoDB key limits
this addon narrows do not exist in SQLite. Moving to AddonTestCase means rebuilding that.
Worth revisiting when core stops mocking Nav in AddonTestCase::setUp().
bootstrap.redundant-registration: The premise does not hold for this layout. AddonServiceProvider::autoloadFilesFromFolder()
is non-recursive and scans `Scopes`, `Query/Scopes` and `Query/Scopes/Filters` only; these
classes live in `src/Scopes/Filters/`, which is never scanned.
The deeper reason the property stays even if they were moved: the parent's scope path runs
after Statamic's own boot sequence, which never fires under Testbench, so `Scope::filters()`
returns nothing in the test suite. bootFilters() registers them the same way and for the
same documented reason as bootCommands(). Registration is idempotent, so the parent
repeating it later costs nothing. tests/Feature/CpFilterScopeTest.php pins the full list, so
an added filter that is left out of the property fails the suite rather than going missing.
ui.page-width: `max-w-5xl 3xl:max-w-6xl mx-auto` with `data-max-width-wrapper` is core's own narrow-page
variant for detail and settings screens — pages/forms/Show.vue:61,
pages/preferences/Edit.vue:14, pages/utilities/Licensing.vue:19, and it is documented as
such in standards/ui-vocabulary.md §2.3. The wrapper carries `data-max-width-wrapper`, so
the header's full-width toggle still applies. The listing page uses `max-w-page`.
The rule reads `max-w-` literally and cannot tell the two variants apart.
